name: Liechtenstein
summary: A tiny Alpine principality, sovereign since 1806, closely tied to Switzerland, known for industry and finance.

knownFor.label: False teeth industry
knownFor.note: A world leader in dental products.

location.value: Between Switzerland and Austria, landlocked; just over 160 km².

terrain.value: About 160 km² in the Alps: the flat Rhine valley in the west and mountains rising to over 2,500 m in the east.

climate.value: Mild for the Alps: the warm föhn wind softens winters in the Rhine valley; colder and snowier in the mountains.

resources.value: Little land and no raw materials; its wealth comes from skilled industry, banking and a favourable tax system.

disasters.value: A flood of the Rhine in 1927 created the Gampriner Seelein lake in the valley.

population.value: 41,237 (2025 estimate, infobox); the article’s body gives 40,542 for August 2026.

urbanisation.value: Small towns and villages: Schaan is the largest, Vaduz the capital; no city has more than about 6,000 people.

disease.value: Very good public health and one of the highest life expectancies in Europe.

migration.value: There are more jobs than residents: about half the workforce commutes daily from Switzerland and Austria.

economicBase.value: A financial sector centred on Vaduz (once a billionaire tax haven, now working to shed that image); electronics, precision instruments, pharmaceuticals and food; Hilti is the largest employer; the corporate profit tax is 12.5%. It has a customs and monetary union with Switzerland.

tradeRoutes.value: A customs union with Switzerland since 1923; part of the European Economic Area since 1995.

wealth.value: One of the richest countries per person.

moneyAndTax.value: Uses the Swiss franc as its currency; low taxes attracted companies and trusts.

inequality.value: Low by international standards; one of the highest incomes per person in the world.

governmentType.value: A constitutional monarchy (the text says semi-constitutional); a 2003 referendum expanded the prince’s powers and the BBC called it Europe’s only absolute monarchy.

keyRulers.value: Hans-Adam II has reigned since 1989 and handed day-to-day government to his son Alois in 2004. Franz Joseph II is not covered in the part read.

succession.value: The Prince is hereditary in the House of Liechtenstein; the people elect the 25-member Landtag.

institutions.value: A Landtag of 25 members elected for up to four years; a constitutional referendum in March 2003 expanded the prince’s powers.

stability.value: Very stable: no wars, no revolutions; the princely family moved to Vaduz in 1938.

eliteConflict.value: Occasional disputes between the Prince and politicians over his powers, settled by referendum.

majorWars.value: The army was abolished in February 1868; full independence followed the German Confederation’s dissolution in 1866. The page says nothing about the World Wars in the part read.

territoryChange.value: Its borders have not changed in modern times.

alliancesRivals.value: Close ties with Switzerland; in the European Economic Area.

inventions.value: Few inventions; companies such as Hilti developed new power tools.

scienceEducation.value: Schools in German; a small university in Vaduz; many students study in Switzerland or Austria.

openness.value: Joined the UN on 18 September 1990; in the European Economic Area since 1995.

communicationTransport.value: Roads and buses; one railway line crosses the country; no airport (Zurich is the nearest).

religion.value: Catholicism is the official state religion. Shares differ: 69.6% Catholic (2020, infobox) and 75.9% (2010 census, text).

languageWriting.value: German is the official language; people speak an Alemannic dialect.

artsArchitecture.value: Vaduz Castle; the Kunstmuseum in Vaduz; the princely family’s great art collection (Rubens and others), shown partly in Vienna.

socialStructure.value: Women gained the right to vote on 1 July 1984, the last country in Europe to do so.

sharedIdentity.value: Loyalty to the princely house and pride in a small, independent state.

dailyLife.value: Houses and flats in villages; Käsknöpfle (cheese dumplings); many people work across the border.

neighbours.value: Switzerland and Austria; it is one of only two doubly landlocked countries.

ideasReligions.value: Shares the German-speaking Alpine culture of its neighbours.

riseSignals.value: Joined the Confederation of the Rhine in 1806 (Treaty of Pressburg, 12 July 1806, per the infobox); fully independent after the German Confederation was dissolved in 1866.

peakPeriod.value: Rapid growth from a poor farming country to one of the richest in the world after 1945.

declineSignals.value: No major decline; criticism of banking secrecy led to tax reforms after 2008.
